Reference SASRec scales input lookups by √d, applies final LayerNorm, and scores against the same, unscaled item embedding table. Therefore m=mean(recent raw embeddings) does not inherit √d scaling; using scaled lookups instead multiplies the residual contribution by √d. LayerNorm is not unit-L2 normalization: learned affine parameters affect h’s norm. Tied embeddings make the mixture exactly s(i)=h·eᵢ+α meanⱼ(eⱼ·eᵢ), adding an embedding-similarity signal whose magnitude depends on learned norms and geometry. These are algebraic implications of the [original model](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py) and [embedding/normalization implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/modules.py).

Average the last min(5, history length) nonpadding interactions; divide by their actual count and return zero for empty histories. Explicit masking remains necessary even with a zero padding embedding: dividing by five attenuates short histories. Verify the loaded padding row, attention masks, sequence alignment, and final valid timestep. Pin implementation revision and run eval mode: [the PyTorch implementation](https://github.com/pmixer/SASRec.pytorch/blob/master/python/model.py) has its own masking and normalization choices. Record whether the residual uses raw embeddings, includes positional vectors, or undergoes normalization after addition.

Recommended diagnostics, inferred from this decomposition: per dataset, report quantiles of ‖h‖, ‖m‖, candidate norms, cos(h,m), α‖m‖/‖h‖, and α·stdᵢ(m·eᵢ)/stdᵢ(h·eᵢ), plus score correlation, top-10 changes, and validation HR@10. Norm matching m to h makes α a relative vector magnitude; matching per-user candidate-score standard deviations makes it a relative score spread. Specify epsilon and zero-vector handling. Cosine scoring also normalizes candidates but changes the baseline; treat it as a separate variant. Raw α values alone are not comparable across datasets.
